# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

Both the legacy billing system ("Old System") and the new billing system ("New System") will run in parallel throughout the migration. Users are migrated in batches; the Old System remains fully operational as a fallback until all migration phases are complete and validated. Decommissioning of the Old System is explicitly out of scope for this plan and must not occur until a separate post-migration phase begins after 100% of users have been on the New System for a full billing cycle with no unresolved critical defects.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (5% of users — 2,000 users)

**Entry criteria before this phase may start:**
- New System has passed end-to-end billing simulation tests (invoicing, proration, refunds, tax calculation) against a shadow copy of production data with 100% output parity against the Old System for a sample of 10,000 historical transactions.
- Rollback tooling exists and has been tested to revert a migrated account back to the Old System within 15 minutes.
- Dual-write/reconciliation monitoring is live between both systems.

**Population:** Internal employees and opted-in low-risk beta customers (e.g., accounts with simple subscription plans, no active disputes, no multi-entity billing).

**Duration:** Minimum 2 full billing cycles before proceeding.

---

## Phase 2: Early Majority (30% of users — 12,000 users)

**Entry criteria before this phase may start:**
- Phase 1 completed with zero critical (Sev-1) billing defects and fewer than 5 Sev-2 defects, all resolved or with approved workarounds.
- Billing discrepancy rate (New System invoice amount vs. Old System shadow-calculated amount) measured at ≤0.1% of transactions during Phase 1.
- Customer support ticket volume related to billing for migrated users is within 1.2x of the baseline rate for non-migrated users.

**Population:** Broader mix of customer segments, including moderate-complexity accounts (multiple subscriptions, standard discounts), selected in randomized batches of ~2,000 users per week to allow incremental monitoring.

**Duration:** Minimum 3 weeks, with weekly go/no-go checkpoints.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (remaining 65% of users — 26,000 users)

**Entry criteria before this phase may start:**
- Phase 2 completed with billing discrepancy rate sustained at ≤0.1% for the full phase duration.
- No unresolved Sev-1 defects for at least 14 consecutive days.
- Finance sign-off confirming reconciliation between New System and general ledger matches Old System reconciliation to within 0.05% variance.
- Customer support escalation rate for billing has returned to baseline (within 1.1x of pre-migration levels).

**Population:** All remaining users, including highest-complexity accounts (enterprise contracts, custom pricing, multi-currency), migrated in weekly batches of approximately 5,000–6,000 users, with the most complex accounts migrated last and given dedicated support monitoring.

**Duration:** 5–6 weeks. The Old System remains active and untouched for at least one full billing cycle after the final batch completes, serving strictly as a read-only fallback/reference system — no decommissioning, disabling, or deletion occurs in this phase or the batch that completes it.

---

## Risks

RISK: Billing calculation discrepancies (incorrect invoice amounts) between old and new systems for migrated users | Run parallel shadow calculations and automated reconciliation diffing for every migrated account for at least one full billing cycle post-migration; auto-flag any diff above threshold for manual review | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Duplicate charges or duplicate invoices generated because both systems remain active simultaneously | Implement a hard cutover flag per account so only one system is authoritative for invoicing at any time, enforced via a shared account-state service checked by both systems before invoice generation | Platform Architecture Team
RISK: Customer data (payment methods, tax IDs, contract terms) fails to migrate completely or accurately, causing failed payments | Run pre-migration data validation checks and post-migration field-level reconciliation reports for every batch before customers are notified of the switch | Data Migration Team
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during a batch migration, delaying resolution of critical issues | Stagger batch sizes, pre-brief support team with known issues and rollback procedures before each phase, and staff additional on-call support during migration windows | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback from New System to Old System for an already-migrated account causes data loss or double billing | Test rollback procedure in staging before each phase and require dry-run rollback validation on a sample account before enabling it in production | Billing Engineering Lead

---

## Halt Criteria

The rollout must be paused immediately, with no further batches migrated, if any of the following occurs:
- **Billing discrepancy rate exceeds 0.5%** of transactions in any 24-hour window for migrated accounts (compared against shadow/reconciliation calculations).
- Sev-1 defect count exceeds 2 open and unresolved at the same time.
- Customer-reported failed or duplicate payment incidents exceed 10 in a single day across the migrated population.

Any halt triggers a root-cause review and requires explicit sign-off from both Engineering and Finance leads before resuming.

PHASES: 3
